issues.description: Using 'var' instead of 'const' or 'let' for variable declarations. The var keyword has function-scoping issues and can lead to bugs with hoisting and accidental reassignment. This appears throughout the file (lines 5-7, 18-20).
issues.suggestion: Replace 'var' with 'const' for variables that don't change (results, all, todo) or 'let' for loop counters. Better yet, use modern array methods like filter() to eliminate the need for manual loop variables.

issues.description: No input validation for the 'query' parameter. If query is null, undefined, or not a string, the code will throw an error when calling indexOf(query), potentially causing the application to crash.
issues.suggestion: Add input validation at the start of the function: 'if (!query || typeof query !== 'string') return [];' This ensures safe handling of invalid inputs.

issues.description: Case-sensitive search using indexOf() may not match user expectations. Searching for 'buy milk' won't find 'Buy Milk', which could frustrate users.
issues.suggestion: Implement case-insensitive search by converting both strings to lowercase: 'if (todo.text.toLowerCase().includes(query.toLowerCase()))' or clearly document that searches are case-sensitive.

issues.description: Using traditional C-style for loops instead of modern array methods. This is more verbose, error-prone, and less readable than functional programming approaches.
issues.suggestion: Replace the entire loop with a single filter operation: 'return listTodos().filter(todo => todo && todo.text && todo.text.includes(query));'

issues.description: The searchTodosByStatus function duplicates the search logic from searchTodos, violating the DRY (Don't Repeat Yourself) principle. This makes maintenance harder as bug fixes need to be applied in multiple places.
issues.suggestion: Refactor to reuse existing logic: 'export function searchTodosByStatus(query, done) { return searchTodos(query).filter(todo => todo.done === done); }'

issues.description: Using 'indexOf(query) !== -1' instead of the more modern and readable 'includes(query)' method introduced in ES2015.
issues.suggestion: Replace 'todo.text.indexOf(query) !== -1' with 'todo.text.includes(query)' for better code readability.

issues.description: Missing JSDoc comments or parameter type documentation. The function parameters, especially 'done' in searchTodosByStatus, lack clear documentation about expected types and behavior.
issues.suggestion: Add JSDoc comments: '/** @param {string} query - The search query string * @param {boolean} done - Filter by completion status * @returns {Array} Filtered todos */'

issues.description: Nested if statements in searchTodosByStatus reduce readability and increase cognitive complexity.
issues.suggestion: Combine conditions using logical AND: 'if (todo.text.includes(query) && todo.done === done)' or better yet, use the refactored filter approach.

codeQuality.summary: The search.js file has several code quality issues. Major concerns include lack of input validation (high security risk), use of outdated 'var' declarations, and code duplication. The code uses traditional loops instead of modern array methods, making it verbose and harder to maintain. While the basic functionality works, the code needs refactoring to follow modern JavaScript best practices, improve security, and enhance maintainability.

untestedPaths.reasoning: This is the main search function exposed via the API endpoint. It processes user input (query parameter) without validation, which could lead to runtime errors if query is undefined, null, or not a string. The indexOf method will throw a TypeError if query is not a string.

Test with a query that matches no todos and verify it returns an empty array. Test with empty string query and verify it returns all todos (since indexOf('') returns 0 for all strings). Test edge cases: null query, undefined query, non-string query (number, object, array) to ensure proper error handling or validation.

If query is undefined, null, or a non-string value, indexOf will perform type coercion which may produce unexpected results or errors. untestedPaths.location: searchTodosByStatus function, nested if condition at line 21-23

refactorings.summary: The search.js file has significant opportunities for modernization and simplification. Key improvements include: (1) replacing var with const/let, (2) using modern array methods like filter instead of for loops, (3) using includes() instead of indexOf(), (4) extracting common logic to eliminate duplication between the two search functions, and (5) implementing a more flexible search pattern that can handle multiple criteria. These changes would reduce code from 28 lines to approximately 15-20 lines while significantly improving readability, maintainability, and extensibility.

issues.description: No validation for the query parameter 'req.query.q'. The endpoint directly passes the query to searchTodos without checking if it exists or is a valid string. This can cause the application to crash when the parameter is missing or malformed.
issues.suggestion: Add input validation before calling searchTodos: 'const query = req.query.q; if (!query || typeof query !== 'string') { return res.status(400).json({ error: 'Query parameter "q" is required and must be a string' }); }'

issues.description: No length limit on the query parameter. An attacker could send extremely long query strings causing performance degradation, high memory usage, or potential denial of service.
issues.suggestion: Add query length validation: 'if (query.length > 100) { return res.status(400).json({ error: 'Query parameter exceeds maximum length of 100 characters' }); }'

issues.description: Missing error handling for the search endpoint. If searchTodos throws an error, the server could crash or return an unhandled 500 error without proper logging or user-friendly messages.
issues.suggestion: Wrap the endpoint logic in a try-catch block: 'try { const results = searchTodos(query); res.json(results); } catch (error) { console.error('Search error:', error); res.status(500).json({ error: 'An error occurred while searching' }); }'

issues.description: No pagination or result limits on the search endpoint. For large datasets, returning all matching results could cause performance issues, high memory usage, and slow response times.
issues.suggestion: Implement pagination with limit and offset parameters: 'const limit = Math.min(parseInt(req.query.limit) || 50, 100); const offset = parseInt(req.query.offset) || 0;' and modify searchTodos to support these parameters.

issues.description: Route specificity concern. While not currently an issue, /todos/search is defined after /todos. If dynamic routes like /todos/:id are added later, proper route ordering becomes important.
issues.suggestion: Keep the current ordering as it's correct (specific routes before dynamic ones), but consider grouping related routes together and adding comments to document the routing structure.

recommendations.description: Add input validation for all query parameters in both search.js functions and the server.js endpoint. Currently, undefined, null, or non-string query values can cause runtime errors or unexpected behavior. Implement validation at both the API endpoint level and the function level.

Create comprehensive test suite for the new search functionality. Currently at 0% test coverage with 2 untested functions and 1 untested API endpoint. Create tests/search.test.js for unit tests and add integration tests for the /todos/search endpoint. Prioritize testing input validation, edge cases, and error handling.

Implement try-catch error handling in the /todos/search endpoint to prevent server crashes. Add appropriate HTTP error responses (400 for bad requests, 500 for server errors) with descriptive error messages. Include error logging for debugging purposes.

Refactor search.js to use modern JavaScript practices: replace 'var' with 'const/let', use array methods (filter) instead of for loops, use includes() instead of indexOf(). This will reduce code size by approximately 40% while improving readability and maintainability.

Add query length validation to prevent denial-of-service attacks. Implement a maximum query length (e.g., 100 characters) in the API endpoint to prevent resource exhaustion from extremely long query strings.

Eliminate code duplication between searchTodos and searchTodosByStatus functions. Extract common search logic into a reusable helper function or refactor searchTodosByStatus to call searchTodos and then filter by status. This follows DRY principles and reduces maintenance burden.

Implement pagination for the search endpoint to prevent performance issues with large datasets. Add limit and offset query parameters with sensible defaults (e.g., limit=50, max=100) to control result set size and response times.

Consider implementing case-insensitive search by default or document the case-sensitive behavior clearly. Current implementation using indexOf() is case-sensitive, which may not match user expectations. Use toLowerCase() on both query and todo.text for case-insensitive matching.
